toegepas.voor: 'n Skuifspeld met 'n laag plastiek of verf om kan die lampie donker hou.
toegepas.na: 'n Skuifspeld wat met 'n laag plastiek of verf bedek is, kan die lampie donker hou.
toegepas.rede_vinder: The dangling 'om' directly before 'kan' makes the sentence hard to parse; a relative clause with a comma reads naturally and keeps the meaning.
toegepas.fout: The particle 'om' lands directly before 'kan', so a reader stumbles on where the noun phrase ends.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The relative clause with 'bedek' reads naturally on a first pass and keeps the same meaning (a clip with a coating around it), with no heading or protected wording touched.

toegepas.na: om genoeg elektrisiteit daardeur te stuur
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'genoeg' has no noun, so the learner must guess what is sent; naming 'elektrisiteit' matches the next sentence and adds no content.
toegepas.fout: 'genoeg' stands without a noun, leaving a Grade 6 reader to infer what is sent through.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Naming 'elektrisiteit' only spells out what is already meant, matches the next sentence, and leaves the protected wording before it intact.

beskerm_bedenkings.woord: Hulle gelei baie swakker as metaal en 'n sel stoot te swak
beskerm_bedenkings.rede: This joins two clauses with their own subject and verb ('Hulle gelei', ''n sel stoot'), so AWS 2017 requires a comma before 'en' ('as metaal, en 'n sel stoot'); I did not propose it because the comma falls inside the protected wording. A person may want to update the protected entry to include the comma.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Two coordinate adjectives before a noun are separated by a comma.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'gebakte klei' works as one unit that 'harde' describes, so the comma is optional and not clearly better.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The previous sentence speaks of 'isolators' in the plural, so the singular 'Die isolator' has no clear antecedent.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: A generic singular 'Die isolator' after a plural is idiomatic Afrikaans, so the change is lateral.
